title: Complete Counterfactual Identification under Signed Monotonicity in Binary Semi-Markovian Models
banked_reason: The district-compositional signed order-AMWN/ctf-calculus with a terminal local-trace compiler was not delivered; the sound global QE/CAD oracle achieved only subfield tier.
gap_reasons: The proposal's district-compositional signed order-AMWN/ctf-calculus with a terminal local-trace compiler is not delivered.

Its if-and-only-if proof uses global response-profile enumeration and real algebraic elimination; it is not a district-compositional order-AMWN or ctf-calculus completeness theorem and does not supply a compiler from a terminal local graphical failure trace.

Districtwise atom probabilities cannot simply be selected independently: the common-menu conditions are globally coupled polynomial constraints, and the current algebraic sample certificate contains no canonical terminal district obstruction. Resolving this requires a genuinely new construction.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a sound finite signed-isotone canonical reduction and a terminating global real-algebraic identification oracle with exact countermodels on failure. It could not replace the oracle with the promised district-compositional order-AMWN/ctf-calculus or compile terminal local failure traces into monotone twin SCMs; repeated bounded attempts discharged none of that load-bearing obligation. The remaining work is a genuinely new local-to-global realizability/gluing theorem and failure-backpointer construction, so the achieved subfield result does not meet the field floor.
tldr: For finite binary recursive semi-Markovian diagrams with signed local monotonicity, the paper gives a signed canonical response-type reduction with Dedekind-number support bounds, a globally complete finite response-profile oracle, a canonical order-normal district factorization, and fixed-branch empirical-cell inference.  The oracle returns an observed-menu functional \(F\) exactly when the conditional counterfactual target is constant on every compatible positive-denominator fiber, and otherwise returns a checkable pair of finite signed-isotone countermodels.  The published \(\mathsf{MID}\) success set is strictly smaller on the common subclass: for \(X\to Y\leftarrow Z\), monotonicity forces \(P(Y_{11}=1\mid Y_{10}=1,Y_{01}=1)=1\) throughout the broader published common-input binary class although published Algorithms 1--2 return \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  What remains open is graphical compression of the global oracle into a terminating district-compositional order-AMWN and ctf-calculus with a local failure-trace compiler.
gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 proves sound monotonicity reductions but explicitly leaves a sufficient-and-necessary general algorithm open. Unrestricted completeness proofs in CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 and RaghavanBareinboim2026 use countermodels whose parity mechanisms violate signed local monotonicity, while canonical finite-SCM programs do not yield a district-compositional identifying calculus.
fill: The project builds a canonical order-normal AMWN representation, proves its district factorization, derives a terminating complete symbolic procedure with explicit state and response-type bounds, and requires every failure to carry two finite order-respecting SCMs and their common menu law. A multisample delta method on a certified locally fixed analytic branch then turns every fixed successful expression into an empirical-cell estimator and confidence interval.
